name: Bhima Riverbank Village Pithla-Bhakri Stalls
area: Bhima river Pune-side bank, Siddhatek temple causeway
signature_dish: Stone-stove bhakri with pithla and village vegetable
why_it_matters: On the Bhima river Pune-side bank near Siddhatek causeway, village women cook unlimited bhakri (jowar/bajra/wheat flatbreads on stone stoves), pithla (gram-flour curry) and a village vegetable for around ₹35-50/meal. Zunka-bhakri is the Maharashtrian farmer's daily food — eating it here is the only authentic-village dining option in Siddhatek. Travel-blog and pilgrim-network documented.
insider_tip: Cash only; no menu, no signage — ask any pilgrim or auto driver for 'bhakri-pithla'. Best 10am-2pm; dries up by 4pm. Sugar cane juice (₹20) is the digestive after the bhakri lunch. Avoid post-monsoon if the causeway floods.
signature_address: Bhima riverbank, Pune-side, Siddhatek temple causeway, Karjat taluka, Ahmednagar 414301

name: Siddhivinayak Temple Trust Prasad Kitchen
why_it_matters: Siddhivinayak temple trust runs a basic prasad kitchen for pilgrims who walk in for darshan via the Pune-side causeway. Subsidised pithla-bhakri-rice meal at near-cost. The only sit-down dining inside the 1km temple radius. Quiet weekday lunches; busy weekend afternoons.
insider_tip: Lunch 12-2pm only; arrive by 12:15. Donation token (₹40-100). Cash only. The Sankashti Chaturthi monthly festival adds a free annadana queue — non-pilgrim travellers may be asked to wait.
signature_address: Siddhivinayak Temple, Siddhatek village, Karjat taluka, Ahmednagar 414301
